Rogers said some minor staff work remains, but issues that fall within the defense committees’ jurisdiction are settled.
Lawmakers aim to unveil the compromise defense bill the week Congress returns from Thanksgiving recess
and begin voting on the measure during the second week of December.
Rogers had initially predicted a bill would be rolled out before Thanksgiving, but said text would be filed the following week “to give staff more time to work on some language nuances.”
“We'll drop the bill when we come back from Thanksgiving, and we'll vote on it week of the eight,” he said.
